verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down in the Pacific Ocean... off the coast of San Diego'; R2: 'splashdown... off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splash down off San Diego’s coast'; R4: 'splash down... off the coast of San Diego, California'; R5: 'splashdown off the California coast'; R6: 'splash down off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'on Friday... April 10'; R2: 'Friday, April 10'; R3: 'Friday... April 10'; R4: 'Friday, April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm the date as Friday, April 10, 2026, with context aligning the year.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down around 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10'; R2: 'around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10'; R3: '5:07 p.m. PST on Friday, April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Direct time matches in PDT/EDT from R1/R2; R3 uses PST but same time, minor timezone notation variance in April (daylight saving period).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will be recovered by the U.S. Navy ship USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha... transport them to the USS Murtha'; R3: 'Navy sailors on the USS John P. Murtha will be responsible for recovering... the crew'; R6: 'the USS John P. Murtha that will bring them home'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly name USS John P. Murtha as the recovery ship for the crew.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft will use parachutes to slow down.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'slow down to roughly 17 mph... thanks to the deployment of several parachutes'; R2: 'deploy its drogue parachutes... three main parachutes... to slow the capsule'; R4: 'three main parachutes are to slow Orion from about 130 mph to just 17 mph'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe parachutes deploying to slow the spacecraft.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft will use an airbag system to upright itself in the water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'five orange airbags will inflate around the top of the spacecraft and flip the capsule into an upright position'
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly describes airbags inflating to upright the capsule post-splashdown; no contradictions elsewhere.
